name: Holland–Dozier–Holland
description:
'''Holland–Dozier–Holland''', often abbreviated as '''H-D-H''', are a songwriting and [[Record producer|production]] team consisting of [[Lamont Dozier]] and brothers [[Brian Holland|Brian]] and [[Eddie Holland]].  The trio wrote, arranged and produced 27 #1 hits for [[the Supremes]], Four Tops, [[Marvin Gaye]], Smokey Robinson and the Miracles, Freda Payne, Jr. Walker & the All Stars and more. The songwriting team wrote 10 #1 hits for the Supremes. They have been credited for being the primary architects of the "Motown Sound".{{better|date=October 2026}}  Eddie, Lamont, and Brian wrote more than 95 [[Billboard Hot 100]] songs.{{citation needed|date=October 2026}}

In 1963, Holland-Dozier-Holland created hits for the Marvelettes (“Locking Up My Heart”), the Miracles (“Mickey’s Monkey”), Mary Wells (“You Lost the Sweetest Boy”), and Marvin Gaye (“Can I Get a Witness”), while achieving their 1st Top 10 pop success with Martha & the Vandellas’ “Heat Wave.” In 1964, the trio propelled one of Motown's newest artists, The Supremes, with their 1st #1 hit, and the 1st of their five (5) consecutive chart-toppers: “Baby Love,” “Come See About Me,” “Stop! In The Name of Love” and “Back In My Arms Again.”  

Holland-Dozier-Holland's work endures in the original recordings and many remakes by others, and some of their songs have become part of the [[Great American Songbook]]. The Rock & Roll Hall of Fame stated that "Motown as we know it would not exist without Holland-Dozier-Holland. Born and raised in Detroit, Holland-Dozier-Holland cranked out hits with the regularity of the auto plants they grew up surrounded by. Yet however machine-like they were in their songwriting, at the core of each hit is a throbbing, aching, unmistakably human heart.".

From 1969 to 1972, due to a legal dispute with Motown, they did not write material under their own names, but instead used the collective [[pseudonym]] "Staff". When the trio left Motown, they continued to work as a production team (with Eddie Holland being added to the producer credits), and as a songwriting team, until 1973.

The trio was inducted into the [[Songwriters Hall of Fame]] in 1988 and the [[Rock and Roll Hall of Fame]] in 1990.
